raw_case_text:
An 81-year-old male presented to the emergency department after suffering a ground-level fall at his workplace. His medical history is significant for hypertension, well-controlled type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, chronic sinusitis on long-term fluticasone, and candida sinusitis treated with topical itraconazole, mupirocin, and budesonide irrigation for 3 months. Prior to the fall, the patient experienced a left-sided headache with left-sided ocular pain and diplopia. The initial physical exam was significant for bilateral proptosis and mild limitation of abduction in his left eye. CT scan of the head (Fig. 1) revealed mucosal disease in the left maxillary sinus and sphenoid sinus with abnormal soft tissue in the pterygopalatine fissure extending into the orbital apex. A follow-up MRI of orbit and brain (Fig. 2) was obtained which showed aggressive sinus inflammatory process within the posterior aspect of the left maxillary sinus with evidence of bone destruction and invasion through the left pterygopalatine fossa, left middle cranial fossa into epidural space, and left orbital floor into intraconal space. A small 8 X 5 x 3 mm left temporal epidural collection with brain edema was visualized as well.
The patient was empirically started on IV liposomal amphotericin B and broad-spectrum antibiotics on first day of hospital admission. He underwent endoscopic sinus surgery, which revealed a fungal ball along the maxillary sinus floor and sphenoid rostrum. Erosion with necrotic tissue was seen along the posterior wall of the maxillary sinus extending into the pterygopalatine fossa and floor of the orbit. The procedure involved the removal of the fungal ball, mucosal stripping of the maxillary sinus, orbital wall decompression, ethmoidectomy, clipping of the distal maxillary artery, and sphenoidotomy. After the procedure, an MRI of the head was repeated which showed post-operative changes with a redemonstration of the epidural abscess in the left middle cranial fossa (Fig. 3). However, it additionally showed a new peripherally enhancing lesion in the left anterior temporal lobe measuring 4 X 7 x 6 mm. Given the extent of the disease, the patient was again taken for a second endoscopic operation for resection of the skull base lesions on hospital day 10. Necrotic debris was removed from the middle cranial fossa and infratemporal fossa with Amphotericin irrigation. Cultures from the endoscopic surgery was consistent with invasive fungal sinusitis and grew Stenotrophomonas maltophilia with Aspergillus fumigatus. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole was added to his antibiotic regimen, and IV liposomal amphotericin B was continued which was then later on replaced by IV voriconazole. However, on hospital day 12, the patient developed auditory and visual hallucinations. Voriconazole was discontinued, and the patient was restarted on liposomal amphotericin B, but the patient developed an acute kidney injury on amphotericin B. The antifungal therapy agent was then changed to isavuconazole. The patient was recommended for a lifelong course of isavuconazole therapy and was discharged to a rehabilitation center on hospital day 34.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 81-year-old male presented after a ground-level fall at work preceded by a left-sided headache, left ocular pain, and diplopia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Prior to suffering a ground-level fall at his workplace, the patient experienced left-sided headache, left ocular pain, and diplopia, prompting emergency department evaluation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Hypertension, well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, chronic sinusitis on long-term intranasal fluticasone, and Candida sinusitis treated for 3 months with topical itraconazole, mupirocin, and budesonide irrigations.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for left-sided headache, left eye pain, diplopia, and ground-level fall.

objective.physical_examination: Initial physical exam revealed bilateral proptosis and mild limitation of left eye abduction.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial head CT demonstrated left maxillary and sphenoid sinus mucosal disease with abnormal soft tissue in the left pterygopalatine fissure extending into the orbital apex. Orbit and brain MRI revealed an aggressive inflammatory process in the posterior left maxillary sinus with bony destruction and invasion through the left pterygopalatine fossa, left middle cranial fossa epidural space (with an 8 x 5 x 3 mm left temporal epidural collection and brain edema), and left orbital floor into the intraconal space. Endoscopic sinus surgery on day 1 revealed a fungal ball along the maxillary sinus floor and sphenoid rostrum with posterior maxillary wall necrosis/erosion; postoperative repeat head MRI showed a new 4 x 7 x 6 mm peripherally enhancing lesion in the left anterior temporal lobe alongside the persistent epidural abscess, requiring repeat endoscopic skull base debridement on hospital day 10. Intraoperative sinus cultures grew Aspergillus fumigatus and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Acute invasive fungal rhinosinusitis with orbital apex, skull base, left middle cranial fossa epidural abscess, and left anterior temporal lobe brain abscess caused by Aspergillus fumigatus co-infected with Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, confirmed by orbital/brain MRI, two-stage endoscopic sinus and skull base surgical debridements (days 1 and 10), and intraoperative cultures. Treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and sequential antifungal therapy: initial IV liposomal amphotericin B was switched to IV voriconazole, stopped on day 12 due to visual and auditory hallucinations, switched back to liposomal amphotericin B which caused acute kidney injury, and finally transitioned to lifelong oral isavuconazole; the patient was discharged to a rehabilitation center on hospital day 34.
